questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Distance from home country and the country being part of EU

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information received upon arrival from the mobility office in Milan was sufficient and very helpful. It was nice to have a direct mail to contact when having questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received emails from the mobility office describing where to go to get the needed signatures and information on how to pick courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through Airbnb, but I was quick and my experience was that there was not that much available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good way to get to know the city around Campus. The city is big and it gives you an opportunity to know it better. I wish I had read more about different areas in Milan before searching for housing around the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received emails throughput the whole process leading up to my arrival in Milan. They consisted of guiding steps which were very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information at the orientation meeting describing the whole process. Here we got to know the coordinator and also received information about who we could contact and where.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. We were able to try different courses before committing to them. It was quite easy to register and the amount of space was unlimited.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read all the information you receive on e-mail, it is very helpful. Talk to other student who are also enrolling in the same problem. Reach out in Facebook group etc. if you do not know anyone personally. This helps if you have day-to-day questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took four courses with different ECTS point. Some of the required more attention, reading and assignments and other required only in-class participation. Overall the level was decent and corresponds to the level on UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was more formal and only lectures, we did not have any TA's or practice classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Data analysis
Digital Society
Journalism, media and politics
Corporate communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend all of the above. Some of the teachers teached more of these classes and they all fit well together.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not enroll in any of these but I know there was an organisation who offered different actives and social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going on trips outside your host city. I enjoyed going on small day-trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stroll around the city looking at cultural monument and do some shopping

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but it gets easier when you get a routine and start attending lectures at the university.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the event organised by the university or connect to other students through different Erasmus groups on social media

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think it was hard not knowing italian. Everything is in italian and translation it not always possible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and welcoming people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient, everything gets easier. You get to know your way around the city, where to buy groceries and get your own favourite places.
2. Do your research on the city, where to go and what to see. It help a lot in the beginning.
3. Plan some trips and visits from home. It gives you something to look forward to when things get hard.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is not anything that comes in mind.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The special and deep friendships I got throughout my stay. And I appreciate getting to know another city as well as my home city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing things on my own and figuring everything out in another country partly alone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
